newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Electric dismisses CLP plan.
newsitem.headline: HK Electric dismisses CLP plan.

text.p: Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd (HEC) on Sunday reiterated it had no intention of buying excess power supply from its competitor China Light & Power Co Ltd.

"HEC states emphatically that China Light & Power should bear the full consequences of their present situation of over-capacity arising from differential between their forecast and actual demand," the utility said in a statement.
"HEC will not purchase power from China Light & Power under any circumstances," it said.
China Light has come under pressure to halt or defer the commissioning of four units at its eight-plant Black Point power station due to a slowdown in growth in electricity demand.
The Hong Kong government asked the company last November to submit a report on the costs of deferring units five to eight of the plant after experts recommended a delay in the original timetable.

But in its report, China Light said the deferral would cost some HK$200 million to over HK$1.5 billion in additional costs and submitted alternative proposals, among them a plan to transfer the excess power to HEC.
HEC said China Light's insistence to build additional plant despite over-capacity had disregarded public interest.

"The increased burden on consumers resulting in higher tariff will adversely affect the well-being of the society, increase the pressure on the government and have a negative impact on the overall economy," it said.
In an initial response to China Light's report, the government last week said more details were needed before an assessment of the proposals could be made.
